column8: goo: molten wax bodies with translucent optics (default). fluid: the older grid fluid simulation.
Named bundle of options (see --list-presets): applied above the saved config file and below environment and command line. Empty = none.
auto: every setting you leave unset is drawn from the seed, so each launch is a different, reproducible lamp. off: unset settings take their defaults.

auto: slow chapters that cross-fade between the others. inside: suspended in the liquid among the wax. glass: eye against the glass. show: a 1960s liquid light show. field: the classic full-screen lamp (lightest). butterfly: Flowerchild, an overhead-projector dye show, saturated and slowly pulsing.
Where the heat comes from: tank (below), dish (one side), radial (a hot centre), drift (gravity swings slowly).
Narrows the palettes drawn when palette=auto: the lamps of a decade, or modern.

Liquid and wax pairing: lamp colour codes of 1992-2004 (code-NN), documented 1960s-1980s pairings (era-NNs-...), the reference photos and videos, the original colourways (way-NN) or a generated pair; auto draws one.
milky: opaque, matte, pitted wax like real lamps. translucent: lit through. jelly: the earlier glossy candy look; opt-in, never drawn.
Strength of the pits, marbling, striations and cooled skin; 0 = smooth.
Metal flecks suspended in the liquid; auto follows the palette (the glitter lamps).
How many flecks.
Density of drifting specks and micro-bubbles.
Strength of reflections, dust and smudges on the glass.
How far apart the depth layers sit and how much the liquid fogs the far wax.
How far the camera wanders; 0 = still.
Light show mirror sectors: 0 or 1 off, 2 to 12 sectors; -1 draws one.
Scales how long each view lasts before cross-fading to the next (views 6-10 min, light show 2-4 min at 1).
1 = the pace of a real lamp (calibrated on real-time footage); higher compresses time.
How thick the liquid is: higher is slower and heavier.
How hard the bulb heats the wax: higher lifts more often.
How much wax is in play in the column.
Cooled wax collects under the top and drips stalactites.
Start as a lamp just switched on: a cold slab that softens, a first column, then the cap.

Light shows (show, Flowerchild). off: the picture fills the whole screen. soft: the projector's round throw with a dark surround. dish: a bright dish on black, pulsing. disc: a larger, brighter, cooler dish (both Flowerchild only). The dish and disc default to a large size that fills most of the screen.

Light shows (dish/disc). 0 = the style's default (about 0.92 of the short side, a large lit disc). Otherwise the radius as a fraction of the short side, 0.30 to 1.00; values between 0.01 and 0.30 are clamped up so the lit area never breaks at the screen edge.

Flowerchild only. off: the dye field unchanged (default). ink: a dark branching ink tree with red droplets over the bright dish. veins: a fibrous vein network where two dyes interdigitate. Never drawn: scenes set it.
Flowerchild only: how strongly the ink tree or the vein network is drawn, 0 to 1.
Flowerchild only: flat colour bands with hard edges and no glow, like a printed poster.
Flowerchild only: extra projectors over the dye. streaks: tall drifting colour streaks. neon: neon-sign tubes. both.
How strongly the beat drives every magmasimplex view. 0 = the pre-beat look exactly (default); the Fillmore live presets raise it.
0 = auto: the virtual beat draws 96..132 BPM and drifts slowly. 60..180 fixes the tempo (used when no audio is driving).

off: a procedural virtual beat, no audio (default). system: listen to the default output monitor (what is playing). mic: listen to the default microphone ONLY when explicitly selected; a log line is printed every time capture starts. Falls back to the virtual beat quietly if capture fails.
fluid engine. Liquid and wax colour pairing, 0 to 29; -1 picks one per run.
auto: light on weak GPUs, full elsewhere. low: light. high and ultra: full (ultra also raises the fluid grid).
Fixes the per-launch randomness so a run can be reproduced; 0 = random.

What draws the pattern geometry. auto: the run or slice seed (the driver's per-slice seed) wins, and a seed that only a scene set is ignored; fixed: a scene that sets seed keeps it as the pattern seed, to reproduce one exact layout.
